bhair-p01.speaker: Kṣemarāja, devotional voice (stotra to cidbhairava)
bhair-p01.question: What is Consciousness-Bhairava, and how does the devotee relate to it?
premises: v1: oṃ namaś cidbhairavāya | citibhūmisamāśrayaṇāś citibhūtiṃ śrayata mā mudhā bhramata | prathayann iti bhaktimatāṃ jayati śivo 'nugrahapravaṇaḥ — salutation to Consciousness-Bhairava; you who seek shelter in Citi — resort to the existence of the power of consciousness; do not wander uselessly. Proclaiming thus, Śiva, intent on bestowing grace to devotees, is victorious.

v2: cidbhairavam eva paraṃ paramāmṛtarūpam ekam atidīptam | ullasitakaraṇacakragrastasamastaṃ śivaṃ vande — I venerate Śiva, the supreme Bhairava of the character of consciousness, solitary, of the form of supreme nectar, radiant, who has devoured the entire existence with the realm of senses streaming out.

v3: stutyaḥ stotā stutir iti yad api vibhinnaṃ na kiṃcid astīha | mṛṣati yathā yad rūpaṃ cidrūpatayā tathā bhavaty etat — here nothing distinct as praised, praiser, praise; as a form appears, so it becomes by consciousness-form.

v4: vigalitasarvavibhedaṃ sarvavibhedātma cidghanānandam | yat tava tattvaṃ bhagavaṃs tasyānukṛtiṃ tvadākṛtiṃ vande — I bow to your form, imitation of your principle, consciousness-dense bliss, all-distinction-dissolved, all-distinction-self, O Lord.

v5: rekhāpuruṣaḥ puruṣaṃ varṇalipir varṇasaṃcayaṃ yadvat | tadvat vicitrarūpaṃ tvām ākāro vyanakti paramātman — as a drawn man reveals a man, script reveals letter-collection, so form reveals you, of varied form, supreme self.

v6: tatrāvikalpam eva tvāṃ cidrūpaṃ samāviśya | vimṛśāmaḥ kim api manāṅ na hi tattvaṃ kalpanāviṣayaḥ — there, having entered you, consciousness-form, without conceptualization, we reflect not even a little; principle is not object of imagination.

v7: svātmaprabhāṃ vidhāya vāgdevīṃ viṣayakusumakḷptārcaḥ | prathamonmeṣaṃ gurum atha vanditvā hṛdayam āviśya — having made speech-goddess one's own light, offering of sense-flowers, then bowing to guru, first manifestation, entering heart.

v8: staumi vimṛśan maheśvaram ātmānaṃ svaṃ cidekaghanam | srāvitapāśakadambakam etasmin dehadevagṛhe — I praise, reflecting, Maheśvara, one's own self, consciousness-one-mass, in this body-temple, having poured out cluster of bonds.

v9: citānandecchāvitkaraṇākhyāḥ śaktayo jayanti vibho | sūkṣmasthūlabhidāptā vaktratvaṃ brahmamuṇḍabhidhā — victorious are powers named consciousness-bliss-will-cognition-action, O Lord; subtle-gross distinctions obtained, face-hood, Brahma-skull named.

v10: sarvajñatādiviṣayaṃ hṛdayādikam aṅgaṣaṭkaṃ te | sakalaṃ sadāśivāntaṃ pretātmatayā tavāsanaṃ svāmin — omniscience etc objects, heart etc six limbs of yours; all up to Sadāśiva, by corpse-self, your seat, O Lord.
bhair-p01.inference: The stotra opens by saluting Consciousness-Bhairava and urging refuge in consciousness rather than wandering in vain. The key doctrine: there is no real distinction between praised, praiser, and praise — every form is consciousness in varied appearance. The devotee bows to the principle and its form, enters it without conceptualization, and recognizes the body as a temple where Maheśa, the mass of consciousness, is praised. It closes by celebrating the powers of consciousness, bliss, will, cognition, and action, and by naming the limbs and seats up to Sadāśiva as Bhairava's own. The fierce iconography is read as philosophical teaching: worldly bonds and distinctions have been cast away. Cidbhairava = cit (consciousness) + Bhairava = consciousness as Bhairava, the self-luminous awareness.
bhair-p01.conclusion: Consciousness-Bhairava is the sole reality; every form is consciousness in varied appearance. The devotee enters the consciousness-form without conceptualization; the body is a temple where Maheśvara (mass of consciousness) is praised. The fierce iconography (skull, bones, etc.) teaches that worldly bonds and distinctions have been cast away. Key: v. 3 (no distinction between praised/praiser/praise) and v. 5 (form reveals the formless, as a drawing reveals a man).
bhair-p01.theorem: cidbhairava = cit (consciousness) as Bhairava; no distinction between praised/praiser/praise; iconography = philosophical teaching (bonds cast away).

Key: v. 3 (no distinction) and v. 5 (form reveals formless). Tone: devotional-philosophical.

bhair-p02.speaker: Kṣemarāja, devotional voice (stotra)
bhair-p02.question: What do Bhairava's weapons and ornaments teach? How is fierce iconography read as liberation-instruction?
premises: v11: paramaprakāśavapuṣo vimarśaśaktiḥ prabho parā devī | asyā eva prasaraḥ sarvā brāhmyādikā devyaḥ — of supreme light-body, reflection-power, O Lord, supreme goddess; her expansion indeed all goddesses from Brāhmī etc.

v12: dahanajalāmṛtalekhāviṣādi bibhrat tvam ādiśasy etat | viśvaṃ viruddham api saccidrūpe mayi virudhyate naitat — bearing fire-water-nectar-ray-poison etc, you indicate this; universe, though opposed, in me of consciousness-being form is not opposed.

v13: saṃvitsūtranilīno niḥsāro mātṛnivaho 'yam | karaṇamuṇḍamālabhārin darśayasītīva naḥ svāmin — consciousness-thread-dissolved, sapless, this host of knowers; skull-garland-bearing, you show us thus, O Lord.

v14: paśyata paśyata pāśā viṣamās ta ime bahiṣkṛtāḥ śaśvat | ity antradhāraṇamiṣat kathayaṃs tvaṃ naḥ samābhāsi — see, see, these nooses are adverse, eternally expelled; saying thus, as if holding entrails, you address us.

v15: māyāpaṭaḥ sarāgo vyomni pare 'smin sa eṣa nikṣiptaḥ | iti gajacarma saraktaṃ mūrdhni vahan kathayasīśa — Māyā-cloth, with attachment, in supreme space, this is cast; thus elephant-skin, bloody, on head bearing, you tell, O Lord.

v16: antaḥśaktikṛpāṇīm vyanakṣi saṃsṛtivibhedinīm asinā | nijaśaktimahimasvīkṛtasamastaviśvā hi vīravarāḥ — you reveal inner power-knife, saṃsāra-splitting, by sword; indeed heroes excellent have accepted all universe by own power-glory.

v17: bhavabhayahantā so 'ham sānāthye 'vasthito 'smi mā bhaiṣṭa | ity āsphoṭitakheṭakadarśanato diśasi naḥ svāmin — destroyer of worldly fear, 'I am established in lordship, do not fear'; thus by shield-display you point us, O Lord.

v18: nijaśaktipāśavalitaś cidvapuṣā kalyate mayā kālaḥ | iti pāśadhāraṇavaśāt prathayasi naḥ kālakālas tvam — bound by own power-noose, by consciousness-body, time is measured by me; thus by noose-holding you show us death of death, O you.

v19: bhedamayam akhilam etan nijaśaktyaivākṣipāmi saṃhartum | ity aṅkuśadhāraṇataḥ sphuṭayati parabhairavo 'smākam — all this is distinction-made; by own power I draw to destroy; thus by goad-holding supreme Bhairava makes clear to us.

v20: kodaṇḍārūdhaśarapradarśanād brahmaviṣṇurudreśān | sasadākhyaśivāñ chaktyā kāraṇahariṇaṃ bhinatsi mṛgavat tvam — by bow-mounted arrow-display, Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra lords, with Sadāśiva, by power you pierce causal deer like deer.
bhair-p02.inference: Bhairava's supreme power (vimarśaśakti) is the supreme goddess (parā devī); all other goddesses are her expansion. The universe, though seemingly opposed, is not opposed in consciousness-being. Each weapon/ornament is a teaching: skull-garland shows the host of knowers dissolved in consciousness-thread; nooses expelled show worldly bonds cast away; Māyā-cloth cast shows Māyā cast away; sword splits saṃsāra; shield shows freedom from fear; noose shows mastery of time (death of death); goad shows destruction of distinction; bow pierces causal roots of Brahma/Viṣṇu/Rudra/Sadāśiva. Fierce iconography becomes direct instruction in liberation.
bhair-p02.conclusion: Bhairava's fierce iconography is not mere description but philosophical teaching: each weapon/ornament instructs in liberation. Skull-garland → knowers dissolved in consciousness; nooses → bonds expelled; Māyā-cloth → Māyā cast away; sword → saṃsāra split; shield → freedom from fear; noose → mastery of time; goad → destruction of distinction; bow → causal roots pierced. Key: v. 12 (universe not opposed in consciousness-being) and v. 16 (sword splits saṃsāra).
bhair-p02.theorem: iconography = philosophical teaching (bonds cast away, distinction destroyed, causal roots pierced).

bhair-p03.speaker: Kṣemarāja, devotional voice (stotra)
bhair-p03.question: How does Bhairava manifest through boon, fearlessness, and power?
premises: v21: varadena pāṇinā tvaṃ viśvavibhūtipradatvam abhinayasi | na khalu paratattvaniṣṭho vibhavamalaiḥ spṛśyate jātu — by boon-giving hand you enact universe-glory-giving; indeed one fixed in supreme principle is never touched by glory-impurities.

v22: abhayena ca bhavabhayāni unmūlayatā prakāśyate satatam | viśvānugrahakāraṇasvabhāvatā tava karatalena — and by fearlessness, uprooting worldly fears, always manifest; by your palm, nature as cause of universe-grace.

v23: akhyātirūpam asamaṃ māyāyāḥ śakalitaṃ śiro 'traitat | parabodhamayena mayā muṇḍaṃ bibhrat prakāśayasy evam — this head, unequal, of Māyā's unmanifest form, shattered; thus you manifest bearing skull by me of supreme awakening.

v24: niḥśeṣahṛtasārā mayy eva jagatsthitiś cidekaghane | iti khaṭvāṅgakaraṅkodvahanacchalato dadāsy ājñām — all essence taken, in me alone world-rest in consciousness-one-mass; thus by skull-staff bone-bearing pretext you give command.

v25: vīṇāghaṇtāḍamarūn uḍḍāmara vādayann idaṃ diśasi | vṛttitribhedabhinnaṃ nādaṃ śṛṇvan sthito 'smīti — playing lute, bell, drum, O Uḍḍāmara, you show this; 'I stand hearing sound divided by three functions'.

v26: kiṃ ca parādikaśaktitritayārāsundarām mahāśaktim | devānukaroṣi bahis triśūladhāraṇamiṣeṇa nityaṃ tvam — moreover, you imitate gods outside, by trident-holding pretext, supreme power beautiful with three powers from Para etc.

v27: icchādikanijaśaktiprakāśitādhaḥsthagocaratritayām | svām eva parāṃ śaktiṃ vajramayīṃ vahasi ṣaḍarāṃ tvam — you bear your own supreme power, diamond-like, six-spoked, three lower realms revealed by own powers from will etc.

v28: jagad akhilaṃ macchaktyā damitaṃ sarvavyāvasthitīr dhatte | iti daṇḍadhāraṇavaśād vyanakṣi cidbhairavāsmākam — entire world subdued by my power, all arrangements bears; thus by staff-holding you reveal Consciousness-Bhairava to us.

v29: mudgaraparaśū bibhrad baindavanādānukārarūpau tvam | bhedavibhedanaśakalanaparatvam īśāna nirdiśasi — bearing mace and axe, of Bindu-sound-imitation forms, you indicate, O Īśāna, state of splitting distinction and non-distinction.

v30: darśanabhedāt svāminn anyānyām āhṛtiṃ dadhānas tvam | bhairavaparabodhamayaṃ prathayasi nijadhāma sarvatra — O Lord, by difference of vision, assuming various forms, you proclaim your own abode, Bhairava supreme awakening, everywhere.
bhair-p03.inference: The boon-giving hand enacts the giving of universal glory; one fixed in the supreme principle is untouched by glory-impurities. Fearlessness uproots worldly fears; the palm reveals the nature as cause of universe-grace. Māyā's form is shattered; the skull is borne by supreme awakening. All essence is taken; world-rest is in consciousness-one-mass; the skull-staff gives command. The three functions (creation, maintenance, dissolution) are heard as sound. The trident imitates the gods; the three powers (icchā, jñāna, kriyā) from Para etc. The vajra (diamond) is the supreme power, six-spoked; three lower realms revealed by will etc. The staff reveals Cidbhairava: the world is subdued by his power. The mace and axe indicate the splitting of distinction and non-distinction. Bhairava manifests his own abode everywhere through differences of vision.
bhair-p03.conclusion: Manifestation through boon, fearlessness, and power: each iconographic element is a teaching. Boon-giving → universe-glory; fearlessness → uprooting worldly fear; shattered Māyā → supreme awakening; skull-staff → command; lute/bell/drum → three functions as sound; trident → three powers; vajra → supreme power; staff → world subdued; mace/axe → splitting distinction/non-distinction; differences of vision → Bhairava's abode everywhere. Key: v. 21 (one fixed in supreme principle is untouched by glory-impurities) and v. 30 (Bhairava manifests his abode everywhere through differences of vision).
bhair-p03.theorem: iconography = philosophical teaching (glory-giving, fearlessness, shattered Māyā, three powers, supreme power, world subdued, distinction split).

bhair-p04.speaker: Kṣemarāja, devotional voice (stotra)
bhair-p04.question: How do purity, inner fire, and formless self relate to Bhairava's iconography?
premises: v31: śāktāṇḍakhaṇḍamadhye viśvarasāḥ sarvam ahaṃ pibāmi sadā | vyañjayasi narakapālagarudhiramiṣād etad iva me 'ntaḥ — in middle of Śakti-egg-fragment, all world-essences, I always drink; by skull-cup blood pretext you manifest this within me.

v32: abhimānahṛdayabandhānutkhātau tāv imau saśikhau | mūrtāv iva muṇḍābjau prathayan dhatse mahākālaḥ — these two, with tufts, excavation of ego-heart-bonds; like embodied skull-lotuses, Mahākāla establishes.

v33: akhilajagadbījabhuvaṃ prathamasthām anukaroṣi bodhanidhe | karatalagabījapūrakadarśanalīlāyitād deva — O treasure of awakening, you imitate first station, seed-place of all universe; by palm-held pomegranate display-play, O god.

v34: bhairavarūpo 'py asi yat tatrāpi kare 'kṣamālikāṃ dhatse | tat sarvākṣavikāsād viśvaṃ parivartayasy antaḥ — though of Bhairava form, there too you hold rosary in hand; by expansion of all letters, you transform universe within.

v35: asthikaramuṇḍamālābhasmābharaṇo nṛraktaruciḥ | viśvaṃ brahmamayatvāc chuddham itīśaḥ samādiśasi — bone-hand, skull-garland, ash-ornament, human-blood-hued; 'universe is pure due to Brahma-fullness', O Lord, you instruct.

v36: svātmārāmamayānāṃ viṣamā api viṣayabudbudhāḥ kim amī | smaradahanam alikanayanam prathayan paramāgnirūpam ādiśasi — for those full of self-delight, what are these adverse sense-bubbles? Manifesting fire of desire, forehead-eye, you instruct supreme fire-form.

v37: antarnibaddhalakṣyaḥ pravikāsikaraṇo 'pi yat sadā bhavasi | tat prathayasi sarvadaśaṃ gatamohakalaṅkam ātmānam — though always with inward-bound target and expanding faculties, that proclaims self free from delusion-stain in all states.

v38: deva digambaratā te vadati nirāvaraṇam ātmano rūpam | paramabrahmamayārkān māyāvaraṇam kathaṃ vṛṇuyāt — O god, your sky-cladness says un-covered form of self; how would Māyā-covering take supreme-Brahma suns?
v39: saṃhartā sarveṣām arkādīnām ahaṃ tamobhūmiḥ | nirmalaśāradagaganaprabheṇa vapuṣeti darśayasi — destroyer of all suns etc, I am darkness-ground; by stainless autumn-sky radiance body you show.

v40: paramabrahmamayas tvaṃ deva yadāśrayasi bhairavākāram | tat prathayasi tattvajñaḥ saty api bhede vimukta iti — you are supreme-Brahma-filled, O god, when assuming Bhairava form; that proclaims knower of principle, though distinction exists, liberated.
bhair-p04.inference: Bhairava drinks the essences of the world within the Śakti-egg fragment; the skull-cup manifests this within. The two (tufts) excavate the ego-heart-bonds; Mahākāla establishes them like skull-lotuses. The pomegranate (seed-place) imitates the first station of all universe. The rosary transforms the universe by expansion of all letters. Bone, skull, ash declare the world pure through Brahma-fullness. Forehead-fire instructs the supreme fire-form. The self is free from delusion-stain in all states. Sky-cladness says the uncovered form of self; Māyā cannot cover the supreme-Brahma suns. The darkness-ground destroys all suns; the stainless autumn-sky radiance body shows this. Even in Bhairava form, the knower of principle is proclaimed liberated despite apparent distinction.
bhair-p04.conclusion: Purity, inner fire, and formless self: skull-cup drinks world-essences; pomegranate imitates seed-place; rosary transforms by letters; bone/skull/ash declare purity through Brahma-fullness; forehead-fire instructs supreme fire-form; self free from delusion-stain; sky-cladness says uncovered form; Māyā cannot cover supreme-Brahma suns; darkness-ground destroys suns; knower liberated despite distinction. Key: v. 35 (universe is pure due to Brahma-fullness) and v. 40 (knower of principle, though distinction exists, liberated).
bhair-p04.theorem: iconography = philosophical teaching (purity through Brahma-fullness, self free from delusion-stain, Māyā cannot cover, knower liberated despite distinction).

bhair-p05.speaker: Kṣemarāja, devotional voice (stotra)
bhair-p05.question: How do retinue, mudra, and effortless worship close the stotra?
premises: v41: vividhaśmaśānamālāvetālāvṛtaḥ prakāśayase | saṃvittiviṣayakalanāmadhyaś citibhairavo 'smīti — surrounded by various cremation-garlands, vetala, you manifest; 'I am Consciousness-Bhairava in middle of consciousness-object-discrimination'.

v42: tvayy evāmṛtalekhā paraśaktimayī parapramātātaḥ | nātha tvam eva jagatām jīvanam iti bhāsi no hṛdaye — in you alone nectar-ray, supreme-power-filled, supreme knower; O Lord, you indeed are life of worlds, thus shine in our heart.

v43: tava śabdarāśivapuṣaḥ pratyaṣṭakam eva bāhyaparivāraḥ | parasūkṣmādivibhedād bhairava lokeśvarapramukhāḥ — of your sound-mass-body, the eight-fold external retinue; from supreme-subtle etc distinctions, Bhairava, world-lords etc.

v44: mudrayati nikhilam etan niḥśeṣasvasvarūpasaṃkramaṇāt | modayati bhaktavargaṃ gatimudaṃ pūrṇatāprathanāt — it seals all this by complete own-form transmission; delights devotee-group by path-joy, fullness-manifestation.

v45: mocayati pāśajālaṃ drāvayati vibhedam īśa te mūrtiḥ | mudrayati vividhasaṃviddraviṇaṃ mudrā tataḥ kathitā — your form releases noose-net, dissolves distinction, O Lord; seals various consciousness-wealth, hence called mudra.

v46: jayati paratattvabhūmipravare nipāyabhūtaiṣa | sphuṭam adhivasatu satattvaprathayā hṛdayasya meyamalam — conquers in supreme principle-ground, excellent, this abode; may it clearly dwell, by true-principle-manifestation, impurity of my heart.

v47: pratikalam udeti saṃvid yā kila tatra sphuraty adho viśvam | śivaśaktivibhavarūpaṃ jānanti maheśa yāgasthāḥ — consciousness arises every moment; indeed there universe flashes below; Mahesha, ritualists know Śiva-Śakti-glory-form.

v48: itthaṃ sphurasi sadā me cidbhairava sarvabhūtātma | tad yāgādijapāntaṃ sampannam ayatnataḥ sarvam — thus you always flash in me, Consciousness-Bhairava, all-beings-self; then all from ritual to japa accomplished effortlessly.
bhair-p05.inference: The stotra closes with Bhairava's retinue, mudra, and effortless worship. Surrounded by cremation-garlands and vetala, Bhairava declares himself consciousness in the midst of consciousness-object discrimination. He is the nectar-ray, supreme knower, and life of worlds, while his sound-body has an eight-fold external retinue. His form releases noose-nets, dissolves distinction, and seals consciousness-wealth as mudra, conquering the supreme principle-ground. Consciousness arises each moment, the universe flashes below, and worship from ritual to japa is accomplished effortlessly. The text's final word: 'Thus you always flash in me, Consciousness-Bhairava, all-beings-self; then all from ritual to japa accomplished effortlessly.' Worship is not by effort but by recognition (pratyabhijñā).
bhair-p05.conclusion: Retinue, mudra, and effortless worship: the mudra (seal) releases noose-nets and dissolves distinction; consciousness-wealth is sealed. Consciousness arises each moment; the universe flashes below. The text's final word: 'Thus you always flash in me, Consciousness-Bhairava, all-beings-self; then all from ritual to japa accomplished effortlessly.' Worship is not by effort but by recognition. Key: v. 45 (mudra releases noose-nets, dissolves distinction) and v. 48 (effortless worship — not by effort but by recognition).
bhair-p05.theorem: mudra = seal that releases noose-nets and dissolves distinction; worship = effortless (by recognition, not effort).
